findingClass: live IPO publishes an open/close date, price band, lot size, or issue size that disagrees with an independent non-ingested oracle
githubIssue: https://github.com/abhayla/IPODhan/issues/199 (G-N, T-472, 2026-09-07): extended from 2 fields (dates only, Chittorgarh oracle) to 6 fields against ipowatch.in, a source the scraper does NOT ingest -- Chittorgarh is ingested (scraper/src/scrapers/chittorgarh-scraper.ts), so comparing against it proved nothing about a scraper defect. The 4 P1s originally cited (subscription understated, band collapsed, Fascinate Textiles priced low) were invisible to a dates-only compare.
failThreshold: any OPEN/UPCOMING IPO whose published openDate, closeDate, priceRangeMin, priceRangeMax, or issueSize disagrees with the value this audit fetches LIVE from ipowatch.in (PRIMARY signal, owned by nothing in our pipeline) - dates compared exactly, priceRangeMin/priceRangeMax/issueSize tolerate a 1% relative difference (ipowatch rounds, e.g. 'Approx Rs 40.88 Crores'). lotSize is ALSO folded into this check's violations, but (T-506, #415, 2026-09-08) no longer compared directly against ipowatch's figure: ipowatch's 'minimum bid is N Shares' line is the MINIMUM RETAIL APPLICATION, not the exchange lot -- since SEBI's 2025 SME rule change that figure is 2x the exchange lot for SME issues (Qualiance International: lot_size=1000, ipowatch=2000, both correct). The lot comparison divides ipowatch's figure by the segment's minimum-application-lot multiplier (SME=2, MAINBOARD=1, findLotDisagreements() in scripts/lib/detection-floor-checks.mjs) before comparing to our exchange lot. See the sibling check a_b_min_application for the direct minimum-retail-application comparison. An unresolved data_conflicts row on a HIGH_VALUE field is a SECONDARY signal. The primary comparison is deliberately independent because the cross-source monitor resolves and re-inserts every row each 30-minute cycle (T-335C), and field_sources.previous_source is populated on 1 of 5746 prod rows so it cannot serve as the oracle.
unverifiableWhen: the ipowatch list-index fetch fails or returns no rows (the check is BLIND, and pages P2); a matched company whose detail page cannot be parsed is excluded from comparison, not silently passed
